cmes.note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 as it is obscured by the pylon. The source may be related to a filament eruption centered near N35W05 which begins to slowly lift off around 2026-07-29T23:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304, GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed from the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery starting as early as 2026-07-29T21:00Z and an EUV wave is seen moving northeast of the eruption site from 2026-07-29T23:00Z to 2026-07-30T03:00Z, indicating northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME observed as a NE halo in STEREO A COR2, and a NW halo in GOES CCOR-1 partially blocked by the pylon. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 not available in real-time due to a downlink gap, but observed as a NW halo here once imagery backfilled. The source is associated with an M1.9 flare from AR 14492 peaking at 2026-07-30T17:00Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. This eruption is also observed as filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304 first lifting as early as 2026-07-30T15:18Z. SDO AIA 171/193 observe brightening, dimming, field line movement, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary shock STEREO A COR2 only analysis.

Updated analysis with available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery, triangulated with STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. This fit is just inside the furthest lobed bumps of the front, capturing the core of the brightest material.
Preliminary bulk STEREO A COR2 only analysis.
Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 using the observed source location, noting eastward deflection.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-30T23:37Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a faint feature in STEREO A COR2 that could be associated, but the leading edge is not trackable in COR2A. This front is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of separate source candidate and because no leading edge could be tracked in STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-31T02:24Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a faint feature in STEREO A COR2 that could be associated, but the leading edge is not trackable in COR2A. This front is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of separate source candidate and because no leading edge could be tracked in STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NNW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-31T03:08Z. While there is not a definite source candidate, this feature could possibly be related to some post eruptive arcades centered around N00W135 seen in STA EUVI 195 and STA EUVI 304 SW of former AR 14493 beginning around 2026-07-31T03:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based only on possible source location N00W135

cmes.note: Very faint feature first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-31T03:24Z. This feature may be seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2, but the image quality is too poor to be sure. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in both SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME may be a filament eruption near the NW limb centered around N40-50W70-80 and best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 193. The filament starts to rise off the disk about 2026-07-31T00:30Z and "snaps" around 2026-07-31T02:00Z, but the majority of the associated material appears to fall back to the disk. Additionally, this CME may simply be outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based only on limited SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and a filament eruption centered around N40-50W70-80 as a potential source.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-31T08:08Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. This is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z. No additional source has been identified for this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the E in STEREO A COR2, and faintly to the W/NW in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely an area of diffuse dimming centered ~S20W35, observed in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-31T12:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, may be observed to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but heavily obscured by overlapping far-sided CME: 2026-07-31T23:00Z and real-time data gaps. The source may be the cluster of AR 14498/14450, closer to AR 14498 as brightening near N15E29 surrounded by some weak dimming and field line movement in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-31T19:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the observed likely source longitude at E29. Front may be visible in GOES CCOR-1 but too muddled by far-sided CME: 2026-07-31T23:00Z to confirm.

cmes.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 until a data gap begins at 2026-07-31T23:24Z. Also visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ends at 2026-07-31T23:38Z. The source for this CME may not be clearly observed, with the only source candidate being on/near the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI, as field line movement around 2026-07-31T17:25Z in EUVI 195 and prominence brightening in EUVI 304 around 2026-07-31T18:45Z as a data gap begins. This source would be around approximately longitude W156.2 with STEREO A at W66.2, and triangulation supports approximately E166, so would be far to be the source match. This CME front was originally analyzed to an on-disk source, updated to be far-sided with more coronagraph imagery available afterwards to triangulate.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 found the previously analyzed LE in SOHO LASCO C2 to fit this triangulation as well, pushing the source to be far-sided rather than the original on-disk source.
SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the source longitude E29, as the best/only observing coronagraph so far.

cmes.note: Very faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-08-02T10:45Z. In real time, this CME was only seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a small piece of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-08-02T09:09Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single view point and beyond-limb source.

cmes.note: CME observed best to the E in STEREO A COR2. Also observed faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 until a downlink gap begins at 2026-08-03T05:00Z, and faintly to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be gradual field line brightening/opening from AR 14501 (S07W43) lasting from approximately 2026-08-03T00:00Z to 2026-08-03T04:00Z in SDO AIA 193/211. The CME is likely deflected northeastward with proximity to the large southern polar coronal hole seen facing STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2, and GOES CCOR-1. The front is notably more faint in LASCO and CCOR-1.

cmes.note: CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is unavailable in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 real-time due to a downlink gap. The likely source is AR 14498, observed in SDO AIA 304 first as a filament liftoff with surface brightening starting around 2026-08-03T07:10Z, followed by a wider swath of faint dimming and brightening starting around 2026-08-03T08:16Z in SDO AIA 171/193, all centered ~N22W12.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using N22W12 as the approximate source, finding some northward deflection. May be some variance in the parameters without other coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

cmes.note: CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption on the south central disk centered around S35W05. The filament in SDO AIA 304 begins to lift as early as approximately 2026-08-03T03:00Z, with most of the eruption seen from 2026-08-03T07:00Z to 2026-08-03T12:00Z, with brightening on-disk. This CME is also observed in SDO AIA 193 as a wide swath of dimming starting at approximately 2026-08-03T10:00Z which migrates southeastward for several hours and covers a large area of the south-central disk. The filament eruption, field line movement, dimming, and brightening are also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 at 2026-08-03T07:55Z and 2026-08-03T08:15Z respectively.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in real-time. The source may be a far-sided filament eruption beyond the NE limb as best seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 imagery at 2026-08-04T06:29Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is also seen in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-08-04T14:00Z. The potential source is not clear, but may be a faint region of dimming seen in the SE of SDO AIA 193 imagery, centered around S40E30, between 2026-08-04T06:00Z-09:00Z. Moving/opening field lines are also visible off the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential estimated source location.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in GOES CCOR-1. Not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap. The source is likely an eruption from approximately N25W30 with dimming, moving field lines, and post-eruptive arcades best seen in SDO AIA 193 and STEREO A EUV 195 starting around 2026-08-04T12:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary measurement based on approximate source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-08-04T20:15Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T06:24Z and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this event is field line movement/opening seen in SDO AIA 171 from beyond the Northeast limb beginning at approx. 2026-08-04T19:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to source beyond the E limb and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

cmes.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NNW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-04T22:00Z. This event is only visible in C2 as it is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this CME is likely far sided beyond the NW limb, but faint field line movement can be seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-04T21:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source from beyond the NW limb and lack of STEREO A imagery to triangulate.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-04T23:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-04T19:09Z. The source of this CME is a filament eruption seen from just beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304beginning at 2026-08-04T22:55Z along with field line opening visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 and limited early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-05T01:26Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely a secondary filament eruption following the filament eruption that caused CME: 2026-08-04T23:48Z. This second filament eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 304 over the NE limb beginning around 2026-08-05T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-08-05T08:15Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps between downlinks for SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, which later backfilled. The source of this CME is likely an eruption centered around N10E40-50 beginning as early as 2026-08-05T05:30Z. Some filamentary ejecta can been seen in SDO AIA 304 as well as a minor EUV wave followed by an area of dimming in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on additional available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.
Very speculative, preliminary single coronagraph measurement based on source location.

The CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C3 at 2026-08-05T18:42Z after a downlink data gap but is out of the field of view in SOHO LASCO C2 in real-time. The source may be an eruption with moving field lines beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting at 2026-08-05T11:30Z.
